A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GeoMix work and have readable text, equations, tables, and figures. v1 includes supplementary Sections A–E; v2 ends after the main references. This identifiable omission supports comparison rather than indicating an extraction gap.

before.justification: v1 reports original GeoMix experiments on four benchmarks, component and training ablations, robustness tests, and supplementary quantitative and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original matching and localization results in main Tables 1–6 and the outlier-sensitivity experiment in Figure 4.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same geometric embeddings, global context nodes, Mix-Training, optimal transport, outlier rejection, and losses. Removing supplementary architectural specifications does not establish a change to the implemented method.

E1.justification: MegaDepth, Cambridge Landmarks, 7Scenes, and Aachen Day-Night remain, including the same training detectors and unseen-detector tests. Removed supplementary experiments use already-covered datasets, scenes, and matching/localization tasks.

E2.justification: GoMatch, DGC-GNN, and A2-GNN lose their reported supplementary matcher-only comparison with GeoMix and the three qualitative comparisons. Comparator membership in all retained main benchmark experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The omitted supplement removes auxiliary evaluation designs: context-node-count sweeps, detector-subset controls, testing without outlier rejection, and matcher evaluation independently of PnP-RANSAC. Settings for the retained main experiments are unchanged; missing implementation disclosures do not establish that those experiments changed.

E4.justification: Supplementary Sections D–E disappear, removing context-node sensitivity, detector-combination and SIFT-bias ablations, matcher-only analysis, the outlier-rejection ablation, and three Cambridge qualitative case studies. These test distinct questions beyond the retained progressive ablation and outlier-sensitivity plot.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retained pose-error quantiles describe errors across examples, not uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Main Table 5 changes GoMatch's MegaDepth AUC@1px from 18.90 to 8.90 under the same reported k=10 setting, placing it below DGC-GNN and A2-GNN on that metric. v2 also removes substantial supplementary results, including GeoMix's matcher precision/recall/F1 of 4.30/8.06/5.40% and the AUC@10px drop from 73.76 to 56.49 without outlier rejection.

T1.justification: Supplementary Section A's explicit definitions of GC-augmented features and bidirectional cross-modal updates, Equations 1–3, are omitted, along with Section B's O(N·Ng) versus O(N²) complexity argument. The main mathematical formulation and losses remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about local/global geometry, multi-detector training, unseen-detector generalization, and state-of-the-art descriptor-free accuracy. Removing supporting evidence does not alter these stated claims.

C2.justification: v2 removes substantive supplementary explanations for complementary GC nodes, modality-specific context, choosing four nodes, low matcher-only scores, attributing gains to detector diversity rather than SIFT reuse, and the necessity of explicit outlier rejection. The main discussion and concluding limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Supplementary Sections A and C supplied unique architecture and reproduction details, including feature dimension 128, encoder depth, attention configuration, Sinkhorn settings, rejection threshold, filtering counts, and Aachen retriangulation and score-merging procedures. These disappear; the main training schedule, hardware disclosure, and code link remain.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain the same. Several references receive publication metadata updates, while the removed supplementary bibliography only repeats works retained in the main references.

P1.justification: The complete five-section supplementary explanatory structure and its separate bibliography are removed, leaving unresolved main-text references to supplementary procedures and results. Main Sections 1–5 otherwise retain their wording; remaining textual edits concern references and the version banner.

P2.justification: Four supplementary tables and three qualitative comparison figures disappear without relocation. They contain distinct analyses and visual evidence. Main figures and table designs remain essentially unchanged, apart from small spacing and reference-page reflow.

improvement.justification: Removing the supplement substantially weakens reproducibility and the evidence supporting detector diversity, context-node choices, and outlier rejection. v2 retains claims and pointers to supplementary material that its PDF no longer supplies. The isolated Table 5 update and bibliographic cleanup do not offset these substantial losses.
